summary: Postinstall downloads and executes binary from a GitHub org unrelated to the package publisher and README
details: @apexfdn/apex@1.0.9 ships a postinstall script (install.cjs) that fetches a platform-specific executable from https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v1.0.0/<asset> and writes it to bin/apex(.exe), overwriting the 0-byte placeholder shipped in the tarball. The CLI wrapper subsequently spawns that binary as the package's entry point. Three attribution mismatches surround the fetch: the package is published under the @apexfdn scope, package.json declares repository github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi, and the README identifies the artifact as @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent — none of which is Apex-Foundation/copilot, the org whose release is downloaded and executed. The release tag v1.0.0 is hardcoded and unrelated to the package version 1.0.9, the fetched bytes are not hash- or signature-verified, and TLS is the only integrity mechanism. Installing the package causes arbitrary bytes controlled by a third-party GitHub org to be downloaded and executed on the installer's machine on `npm install`, and again whenever the `apex` CLI is invoked.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
